methodological_rigor.justification: This is an open-label, single-arm phase I dose escalation and expansion trial (parts I and J of SERENA-1) with a total of 29 participants—appropriately sized for phase I safety and tolerability objectives. DLT evaluation period is clearly defined, and CTCAE grading is applied. PK analysis with population PK comparisons to CAPItello-291 is informative. The major methodological limitation is the small, non-randomized sample size, which precludes definitive efficacy conclusions. The ctDNA biomarker analysis (ESR1m clearance in 92% of 12 evaluable patients) is exploratory. The subgroup analyses by ESR1m and PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN status are underpowered for comparison.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This study addresses a clinically high-priority question in advanced ER+/HER2- breast cancer: whether camizestrant, a next-generation oral SERD now demonstrated superior to fulvestrant, can be combined with capivasertib (approved with fulvestrant) with an acceptable safety profile. The combination potentially replaces the fulvestrant+capivasertib standard with a more effective SERD. Preliminary efficacy (ORR 37%, CBR24 52%, mPFS 8.3 months) in a heavily pretreated population including 90% CDK4/6i-pretreated patients is clinically meaningful. The ESR1m ctDNA clearance data provide direct mechanistic pharmacodynamic evidence.

reporting_quality.justification: Phase I trial reporting standards are well met: DLT criteria, participant flow, baseline characteristics, AE table by preferred term with grade breakdown, PK data with comparison to popPK models, and efficacy with CIs. The ctDNA methodology is described by reference to the previously published SERENA-1 monotherapy paper. Limitations are transparently reported including the PTEN detection limitation of the assays used. Supplementary materials are referenced but redacted. No data sharing statement.

novelty_literature.justification: This study evaluates a clinically logical combination (camizestrant + capivasertib) that extends the camizestrant clinical development program. The key novel contribution is demonstrating that capivasertib can be combined with camizestrant without unexpected PK interactions or additive toxicity, enabling phase III evaluation. However, combination SERD+PI3K/AKT inhibitor strategies are not conceptually novel (fulvestrant+capivasertib is approved), and the study does not provide mechanistic insights beyond safety/PK confirmation of a predictable combination.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is concisely written with clear separation of safety, PK, and efficacy results. Tables and figures effectively communicate the data. The discussion appropriately places results in context of the broader camizestrant development program and explains the rationale for the combination. Limitations including the non-randomized single-arm design and small sample size are acknowledged. The ESR1m ctDNA figure is particularly informative and well presented.

key_strengths: First prospective data combining camizestrant with capivasertib, demonstrating absence of clinically relevant PK drug-drug interaction and safety profile consistent with each monotherapy
Encouraging preliminary efficacy (ORR 37%, CBR24 52%, mPFS 8.3 months) in a heavily pretreated population with 90% CDK4/6i prior exposure
Strong ESR1m ctDNA clearance (92% with ≥50% reduction, 67% complete clearance) provides pharmacodynamic evidence of ER target engagement
key_concerns: Non-randomized single-arm design (n=29) precludes efficacy comparisons with fulvestrant+capivasertib or other combinations
Very small subgroup analyses for ESR1m and PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroups (n=11-17) are insufficient for reliable biomarker-efficacy conclusions
Two DLTs from capivasertib occurred (grade 3 rash), requiring careful management guidance for phase III trials
PTEN loss detection limitation in the ctDNA assay may have underclassified PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alteration prevalence, affecting the biomarker subgroup results
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a well-executed phase I report from a high-priority drug combination in advanced breast cancer that provides the safety, PK, and preliminary efficacy foundation needed for phase III evaluation; it meets Tier 2 standards as first clinical data for this drug combination, with minor clarifications needed on DLT management protocols and PTEN detection limitations.
